title: Turn interviews into a product decision
desc: For a researcher or product manager with notes but no agreed next move.
inputs: Interview notes or transcripts, the research question, and the decision you need to make.
prompt: Use these interview notes to identify supported needs, frame the underlying job, and recommend which problems deserve investigation next.
outcome: Findings tied to source passages, a job statement, and a prioritized set of problems with the evidence gaps visible.

steps.why: Extract supported findings and disagreements from the interviews.
Use those findings to describe the progress the person is trying to make.
Compare the resulting problems using a suitable framework and the evidence available.

note: If you only have internal opinions, use them as hypotheses. They cannot stand in for interview findings.

title: Make a feature idea ready to discuss with engineers
desc: For a product owner, founder or designer who needs behavior defined before implementation.
inputs: The user problem, existing product behavior, constraints, and any research or support evidence.
prompt: Turn this feature idea into a specification with user flows, edge cases and testable acceptance criteria. Identify the decisions we still need to make.
outcome: A feature specification that explains the user problem, intended behavior, constraints and acceptance criteria.

steps.why: Check the current product evidence and identify the release decision the feature serves.
Translate that context into flows, states, rules and acceptance criteria.
If sequencing is part of the decision, show the feature alongside dependencies and other planned work.

note: A small, well-understood change can start at Write feature spec. A roadmap is optional when you only need one specification.

title: Fix a website people cannot find their way around
desc: For a designer, founder or content owner reviewing a confusing site.
inputs: A URL, sitemap or page inventory, the main visitor tasks, and any search or usability observations.
prompt: Review this site against the tasks visitors need to complete. Propose clearer navigation and labels, then prepare a usability study to test the changes.
outcome: A proposed site structure, the reasons behind its labels, and research tasks that can test whether people find the right content.

steps.why: Compare the content structure with visitor tasks and propose navigation and labels.
Turn the risky navigation assumptions into neutral participant tasks.
Check the specified interface for barriers that could prevent people using the navigation.

note: You can begin with a page inventory. Usability findings require actual participant observations; an agent walkthrough is not a substitute.

title: Find the gaps in an everyday business process
desc: For an operations lead improving approvals, onboarding or another recurring handoff.
inputs: An existing SOP, staff notes, forms, system exports or a description of what happens today.
prompt: Map how this process currently works, including triggers, owners, systems and exceptions. Show the handoffs that need clarification and propose improvements.
outcome: A sourced current process, unresolved ownership questions, and proposed changes with the assumptions identified.

steps.why: Document the actual steps and exceptions, or use optimization mode to investigate improvement opportunities.
Where the experience matters, connect those steps to the people involved and the systems supporting them.
Compare the proposed fixes using agreed criteria instead of treating every issue as equally urgent.

note: Use only the first skill for an SOP. For a sales process spread across CRM exports and discovery files, use Map sales process instead.

title: Choose a sprint the team can actually commit to
desc: For a team lead or product owner with more backlog than capacity.
inputs: Backlog items, the definition of ready, team availability, estimates and dependencies.
prompt: Review this backlog for readiness, then propose a sprint goal with commit and stretch work that fits our available capacity.
outcome: Readiness gaps, a sprint goal, a capacity-based commitment and explicit stretch work.

steps.why: Identify unclear, oversized or blocked items before selecting the sprint.
Size the commitment against each person’s available capacity and the sprint goal.
During delivery, record status, risks and decisions against the accepted plan.

note: If estimates or capacity are missing, establish them before presenting a firm commitment. Status reporting is an ongoing follow-up, not a prerequisite to planning.

title: Start and validate a signed client project
desc: For a project manager receiving work from a sales or account team.
inputs: The signed scope, confirmed commercials, delivery owners, constraints and the handoff material available.
prompt: Check the handoff for this signed engagement, prepare kickoff and the first delivery plan, and identify what we will need for acceptance.
outcome: An accepted handoff, kickoff and delivery records, and an approach to testing the agreed requirements.

steps.why: Resolve the receiving owner and assemble the signed scope, decisions and delivery constraints.
Use the accepted handoff to prepare kickoff, project records and initial planning.
As work becomes testable, trace tests and UAT evidence back to the requirements.

note: This is a lifecycle path, not a request to perform every stage immediately. Missing signed scope or an unaccepted handoff needs resolution before kickoff is treated as ready.

title: Develop or review a Salesforce feature with Claude
desc: For a developer working on Apex, triggers or LWC in an existing repository.
inputs: The repository or relevant files, the requested behavior, and the project instructions and tests available.
prompt: Review this Salesforce change against the project’s conventions. Keep business logic reusable across entry points, explain design issues and prepare the change for the configured delivery checks.
outcome: A code change or specific review findings, architecture checks, and the applicable delivery evidence.

steps.why: Read existing conventions, then review or implement the service, query, transaction and controller responsibilities.
When the change is ready for delivery, use the project’s worktree and verification workflow.

note: No specially named architecture document is required. Configure Salesforce project is a separate option when you want to install or repair repository standards and Claude hooks; do not run it just to review code.

title: Set up or repair a Salesforce repository’s Claude hooks
desc: For a maintainer who wants consistent checks in the development workflow.
inputs: The Salesforce repository, existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, hook configuration, and the standards the team has adopted.
prompt: Audit this Salesforce repository’s delivery standards and Claude hooks. Preserve working configuration, explain gaps, and repair the agreed checks.
outcome: A standards audit or repaired repository setup, with the changed hooks and checks verified.

steps.why: Inspect the current setup and apply the selected install, audit or repair operation.
Use a real Apex or LWC change to inspect how the agreed architecture applies to code.

note: Choose audit when adoption is undecided. A repository configuration change does not authorize a Salesforce organization deployment.

title: Run an existing Salesforce release pipeline
desc: For a release owner operating a repository that already uses sf-deploy-engine.
inputs: The repository, pipeline.yml, target environment, configured authentication and the requested validation or deployment operation.
prompt: Check the configured Salesforce pipeline and target environment, then run the authorized validation and report the evidence and any blockers.
outcome: The requested pipeline result, target identity, validation or deployment evidence, and a clear failure report if it cannot proceed.

steps.why: Use the existing pipeline’s environment checks and selected validation or deployment path.

note: This route requires an existing pipeline. For a team using Salesforce DevOps Center instead, use Manage Salesforce DevOps and its promotion mode; the two tools are alternative delivery paths.

title: Prepare a useful next conversation with a prospect
desc: For a seller or consultant who needs a focused conversation rather than a generic pitch.
inputs: The account context, prior discovery notes, current offering descriptions and the decision the next call should advance.
prompt: Use this account context and discovery evidence to prepare the next call. Identify the open questions and assess which offering fits, with evidence for the recommendation.
outcome: A focused call plan, supported fit assessment and the questions that still need an answer.

steps.why: Use the account context to prepare the pursuit record or one upcoming call.
After the conversation, turn the notes into supported findings and unresolved questions.
Compare the findings with the actual offering criteria and explain the fit.

note: Offering fit requires supplied offering definitions. Do not assume a stranger uses Megan’s or a former employer’s service catalog.

title: Compare project options before writing an agreement
desc: For a consultant or account lead choosing what to include in a proposal.
inputs: Candidate scope, assumptions, effort and staffing information, commercial inputs and the relevant contract profile.
prompt: Develop and compare these scope options. Explain inclusions, exclusions, effort and tradeoffs, then draft the selected statement of work from confirmed terms.
outcome: Comparable scope options and, once the choice and terms are confirmed, a statement-of-work draft.

steps.why: Build the scope, effort and staffing assumptions behind the options.
Make the options and their tradeoffs comparable in the requested format.
Use the confirmed selection, commercials and contract profile to draft the agreement.

note: A statement of work needs confirmed terms. Use Review deal economics if provider margin and approval conditions are also part of the decision.

title: Prepare an application for a specific role
desc: For a job seeker turning a verified career record into a focused application.
inputs: The job description, career evidence, current resume, preferred career direction and any writing profile you want applied.
prompt: Assess this role against my goals, then prepare the application. Tailor my resume and supporting materials using only the experience and results my sources support.
outcome: A role assessment, role-specific application record, tailored resume and supporting draft materials.

steps.why: Compare the role with the candidate’s chosen progression path and decision gates.
Establish the role interpretation and application context from the supplied career record.
Apply the role context to resume wording and supported figures.
Prepare the requested cover letter, outreach or other supporting copy.

note: Resume tailoring and application materials are modes included in Prepare job application. Other people supply their own career evidence; these skills do not need Megan’s private records. Submission remains a separate authorized action.

title: Turn a project into a portfolio case study
desc: For a designer, product professional or consultant explaining their own work.
inputs: The project evidence, personal contribution, decisions, approved outcomes and publication or confidentiality constraints.
prompt: Turn this project into a case study that explains the problem, my contribution, the decisions and the supported outcome. Identify anything that needs permission before publication.
outcome: A case-study draft and approved public translation, with claims checked against the project evidence.

steps.why: Separate the person’s contribution and supported results from the wider project history.
Improve clarity and the selected voice while preserving the supported claims.

note: Use Develop independent product first only if you want to create a company-neutral product or offer from historical work. It is not a prerequisite to writing a case study.

title: Improve a draft without losing its meaning
desc: For anyone editing a report, article, email or internal document.
inputs: The draft, intended reader, purpose, required facts and an optional confirmed author-style profile.
prompt: Review this draft for clarity and repetition. Preserve its meaning, qualifications and voice, and explain any change that needs my judgment.
outcome: A revised draft, with material meaning changes or unresolved choices made visible.

steps.why: Inspect the sentences and argument, repair the writing, and preserve facts and voice.

note: A private writing profile is optional. Use Manage writing profile only when you want to create or revise an explicitly chosen person’s profile.

title: Build a presentation that supports a decision
desc: For a team lead, founder or consultant briefing an audience.
inputs: The audience, the decision, source material, supported numbers and any confirmed brand or template.
prompt: Build a briefing deck for this audience and decision. Use the supplied evidence to explain the options and recommendation, with visuals that clarify the argument.
outcome: A presentation whose structure, claims and visuals support the audience’s decision.

steps.why: Choose the argument and slide structure from the audience decision and available evidence.
Check the finished deck against the sources, requested task, writing and rendered format.

note: A confirmed brand is an input when branding matters. The workflow can use its neutral profile when no brand is supplied; it does not need a former employer’s identity.

title: Take a sticker idea through design and sheet layout
desc: For a maker developing typography-led stickers for printing.
inputs: The message, intended size, visual references and production constraints; later, the approved PNG designs.
prompt: Explore distinct sticker compositions for this message and size. Once I choose a design and supply the approved PNGs, lay them out as Cricut Print Then Cut sheets.
outcome: Design directions and selected artwork, followed by print-sheet files made from the approved designs.

steps.why: Develop and critique the composition, type and production fit before settling on artwork.
Arrange the supplied PNGs using the available project generator and print constraints.

note: Sheet layout needs actual approved PNGs and the supported generator. It does not create a physical test print or confirm that a cutter accepted the files.

title: Answer a game question from your own planner
desc: For a Fortune’s Weave player checking a route, roster or planning decision.
inputs: The current route, roster and planner or other project sources, plus the question you want answered.
prompt: Use my current Fortune’s Weave planner to answer this question. Separate what the game sources establish from any planning recommendation, and propose a planner update if needed.
outcome: A source-based answer or a scoped planner update using the player’s current project.

steps.why: Resolve the current game and planner sources before answering or changing the requested record.

note: Another player supplies their own route and planner context. If those sources are absent, establish the project context instead of using Megan’s history.

title: Resume a project after a break
desc: For someone returning to an ongoing project or handing it to another assistant.
inputs: The project folder or configured knowledge system, current decisions, and any previous handoff.
prompt: Find the current project state and controlling sources. Explain what is complete, what is open and the next useful action, then prepare a handoff another session can use.
outcome: A current context summary and a handoff tied to the actual project sources.

steps.why: Read the available subject authorities and distinguish current facts from historical records.
Capture the state, source references and exact remaining work for the next session.

note: Connected retrieval needs the person’s configured knowledge system. Supplied project files can provide context where supported; the skill does not grant access to someone else’s private Hub.

title: Package a repeated workflow as a reusable skill
desc: For someone maintaining their own skills collection.
inputs: The repeated task, representative inputs and outputs, failure cases, and the target host or existing estate checkout.
prompt: Turn this repeated workflow into a skill with clear triggers, required inputs, examples and failure behavior. Verify its package for the target host and explain its dependencies.
outcome: A source skill and checked package that preserve the actual workflow and required resources.

steps.why: Define and implement the workflow using the estate’s authoring mode.
Compare the result with representative inputs, expected outputs and the requested behavior.
Prepare and inspect the target-host package through the maintenance skill’s release mode.

note: Authoring and release are modes of Maintain skills estate. Estate maintenance requires the selected checkout; packaging is separate from installation or an account upload.
